ai.description: This 40–50 mm toad is brown with dark dorsal markings and a pale belly. It features prominent horn-like skin projections on the upper eyelids and a distinct dark triangular patch behind the eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys wuliangshanensis* is distinguished by the presence of a distinct, elongated, horn-like dermal projection on each upper eyelid, which is absent in similar Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys wuliangshanensis* is not found in the Indian subcontinent; it is endemic to high-altitude evergreen forests in China’s Wuliang Mountains, typically above 2,000m.
ai.behavior: The Wuliangshan horned toad is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter to ambush passing insects under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys wuliangshanensis* is not found in India; it is endemic to China. It breeds in streams during the summer, laying small clutches of pigmented eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Wuliangshan Horned Toad is not found in the Indian subcontinent; it is endemic to the Wuliang Mountains in Yunnan, China, at elevations of 1,800–2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Wuliangshan Horned Toad emits a low-pitched, single-note "cluck" repeated at slow intervals, typically heard near small, rocky streams within dense montane forests.
